research_input.frequency: FREQUENCY.md: AWS Backup has no rank of its own; it sits inside 'DR strategies and RTO/RPO' (rank 16 of 42, moderate to strong). Pair to decide: AWS Backup vs native snapshots (central policy, cross-account and cross-Region copies, Vault Lock). Stem signals: 'cannot be deleted or modified', 'WORM' (Backup Vault Lock, or S3 Object Lock in chapter 21), 'central backup policy across accounts', 'RPO' and 'RTO'. DR strategies themselves are taught in chapter 40; this chapter owns backup and restore and the backup plan mechanics.

research_input.naming: Current names: AWS Backup, AWS Backup Vault Lock, AWS Backup Audit Manager, logically air-gapped vault, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive. Former name to mention at most once: Amazon S3 Glacier Vault Lock is a different feature (S3 Glacier vaults service closed to new customers, fact s3-glacier-change-vault-service-closed-2025-10).
research_input.story: STARTUP.md chapter 24 (stage 3, month 22): the bank asks for the backup policy, proof of last month's backups and a restore test. Data in Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS and EBS across several accounts, each with different backup settings. Bank requires daily backups kept 30 days and monthly backups kept 7 years; administrators must not be able to delete backups. Adds: AWS Backup plans by tag, backup vault with Vault Lock, cross-account copy; stage 4 cross-Region copy. Decision: AWS Backup for the whole organization; accepts a second policy layer and the storage cost of seven-year copies. Chen asks whether an attacker with administrator access in production can delete the backups. Story numbers are story data, never facts.
